title: Run policy
description: The document that narrows what one run may do. Read once from a file outside the checkout, or from the security_policy of a server's run configuration, and pinned for the run. It can only tighten what the runner binary allows; it never grants: a credential, a tool or an image it selects is one the machine defines, and it defines none.

version.description: The policy format. A runner refuses a version it does not read.

egress.description: What the session may reach through the runner's proxy.

mode.description: observe records every connection and denies only what deny covers; enforce denies a connection to a host outside allow as well, and records the denial. Enforce with no allow list reaches nothing.

allow.description: Hosts the session may reach: a lower-case host name, or a *. suffix matching every host below it and not the apex itself. No ports, no paths, no schemes: paths have a key of their own. Absent means an empty list.

deny.description: Hosts the session may not reach, in allow's grammar, in either mode: a host an entry here covers is denied before allow and before the mode are consulted, and the denial is recorded with the entry as its rule. Absent means an empty list.

paths.description: The paths the session may request on a host, by host in allow's grammar. A host listed here is one the proxy terminates TLS for, behind a wall, because a path is inside the connection: a request whose path no entry matches is denied under enforce and recorded either way, and a host not listed is reached on every path. A path is compared as the server reads it, case and all; a request whose path could be read two ways is denied.

additionalProperties.description: An empty list is no path of the host at all.

credentials.description: The credentials of the machine's this run may use, by name, behind a wall. The runner keeps each outside the enclosure and the proxy sets it on the requests to the hosts it is for, which it terminates TLS for; the session's environment and files contain at most a placeholder for it. A name the machine does not define is no run.

argument.description: What the run requests of the credential, such as a repository, passed to the definition's adapter as one argument. The definition sets what an argument may look like; one it does not provide for is no run. At most 4096 characters, which leaves room for several repositories in one argument, acme/shop,acme/lib. The cap bounds only the size of the run's record, not what the argument may contain: what guards it is the definition's pattern, which must match it whole, and it reaches the program as one word, with no shell.

tools.description: The tools of the machine's this run may reach, by name, behind a wall. The runner starts each for the run outside the enclosure; the proxy terminates TLS for the hosts it serves and sends it every request to them that it allows, including under observe those whose path no rule covers, which are recorded as allowed with an empty path_rule. A name the machine does not define is no run.

argument.description: What the run requests of the tool, such as a repository or a prefix, passed to the definition's command as one argument. The definition sets what an argument may look like; one it does not provide for is no run. At most 4096 characters, which leaves room for several repositories in one argument, acme/shop,acme/lib. The cap bounds only the size of the run's record, not what the argument may contain: what guards it is the definition's pattern, which must match it whole, and it reaches the program as one word, with no shell.

image.description: The image of the machine's the run starts in, by name, behind a wall. The machine defines its images, a reference and the runtime the wall starts it under; the policy selects one and contains no reference. Absent means the machine's default. A name the machine does not define is no run, and the image is fixed when the run starts.

path.description: A path from the root, matched whole, or up to a final * matched as a prefix: /repos/acme/shop, /repos/acme/shop/*. No other wildcard, no query.
